purpose.statement: EMPPAY is a standalone batch COBOL program authored by Ashis Kumar Naik that calculates an employee's weekly and monthly gross pay, applying overtime and reward bonus multipliers, then displays the results to standard output. The program runs a single fixed employee record through initialization, weekly pay computation, monthly pay computation, and output display before terminating.

code_references.snippet:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. EMPPAY.
       AUTHOR. ASHIS KUMAR NAIK.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM INITIALIZATION.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           PERFORM SHOW-OUTPUT.
           STOP RUN.

business_rules.statement: An employee's first name defaults to 'FRANCISCO' at data definition time but is immediately overridden during INITIALIZATION to 'Millard', last name to 'Fillmore', hours worked per week to 19, and hourly rate to $23.50. These are the operative input values for all subsequent calculations.

code_references.snippet:
05  EMP-NAME.
                10 EMP-FNAME        PIC X(15) VALUE 'FRANCISCO'.

INITIALIZATION.
           MOVE "Millard"           TO EMP-FNAME.
           MOVE "Fillmore"          TO EMP-LNAME.
           MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – Overtime Rate Tier 1: If an employee works 40 or more hours in a week, an overtime multiplier (EMP-OT-RATE) of 0.25 (25%) is applied to the total pay calculation.

code_references.snippet:
IF  EMP-HOURS >= 40
               MOVE .25 TO  EMP-OT-RATE

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – Overtime Rate Tier 2: If an employee works 50 or more hours in a week, an overtime multiplier of 0.50 (50%) is applied. NOTE: Due to the ELSE-IF structure evaluated after the >= 40 check, this branch is logically unreachable; hours >= 50 will always match the >= 40 condition first, making the 50% tier a dead code defect.

code_references.snippet:
ELSE IF EMP-HOURS >= 50
               MOVE .50 TO EMP-OT-RATE
           ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-OT-RATE.

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – No Overtime: If an employee works fewer than 40 hours in a week, no overtime premium is applied (EMP-OT-RATE = 0).

code_references.snippet:
ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-OT-RATE.

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – Weekly Gross Pay Calculation: Weekly gross pay is computed as (Hours Worked × Hourly Rate) multiplied by (1 + Overtime Rate). This means the overtime rate acts as a percentage uplift on total weekly earnings rather than an incremental rate on only excess hours.

code_references.snippet:
COMPUTE EMP-PAY-WEEK =
                (EMP-HOURS * EMP-HOURLY-RATE) * (1 + EMP-OT-RATE).

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – Monthly Reward Bonus: If an employee works more than 150 hours in the week (EMP-HOURS > 150), a reward bonus multiplier (EMP-REWARD) of 0.50 (50%) is added to the monthly pay calculation.

code_references.snippet:
IF  EMP-HOURS > 150
               MOVE .50 TO  EMP-REWARD

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – No Monthly Reward: If the employee does not exceed 150 weekly hours, no reward bonus is applied (EMP-REWARD = 0).

code_references.snippet:
ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-REWARD.

business_rules.statement: Business Rule – Monthly Gross Pay Calculation: Monthly gross pay is computed as (Weekly Gross Pay × 4) multiplied by (1 + Reward Rate). This assumes exactly 4 weeks per month and applies the reward bonus as a percentage uplift on the annualized base.

code_references.snippet:
COMPUTE EMP-PAY-MONTH =
                (EMP-PAY-WEEK * 4) * (1 + EMP-REWARD).

inputs.statement: All input data is hard-coded in WORKING-STORAGE. EMP-RECORD is the sole data structure, containing employee name (EMP-FNAME, EMP-LNAME), hourly rate (EMP-HOURLY-RATE, PIC 9(3)V99), overtime rate (EMP-OT-RATE, PIC V99), reward rate (EMP-REWARD, PIC V99), and weekly hours (EMP-HOURS, PIC 9(3)). There are no external file, database, or queue inputs.

code_references.snippet:
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       77  REC-COUNTER              PIC 9(1).
       01  EMP-RECORD.
           05  EMP-NAME.
                10 EMP-FNAME        PIC X(15) VALUE 'FRANCISCO'.
                10 EMP-LNAME        PIC X(15).
           05  EMP-HOURLY-RATE      PIC 9(3)V99.
           05  EMP-OT-RATE          PIC V99.
           05  EMP-REWARD           PIC V99.
           05  EMP-HOURS            PIC 9(3).
           05  EMP-PAY-WEEK         PIC 9(7)V99.
           05  EMP-PAY-MONTH        PIC 9(7)V99.

outputs.statement: All output is written to standard output (SYSOUT) via DISPLAY statements. Six data fields are displayed: employee full name, weekly hours, hourly rate, overtime/bonus rate, weekly gross pay, and monthly gross pay. An additional hard-coded personal message is also displayed.

code_references.snippet:
SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".

processing_logic.statement: Step 1 – Program Entry: Control enters the PROCEDURE DIVISION and sequentially PERFORMs four paragraphs (INITIALIZATION, PAYMENT-WEEKLY, PAYMENT-MONTHLY, SHOW-OUTPUT) before issuing STOP RUN.

code_references.snippet:
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM INITIALIZATION.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           PERFORM SHOW-OUTPUT.
           STOP RUN.

processing_logic.statement: Step 2 – Initialization: Employee demographic and rate data are loaded into WORKING-STORAGE fields. Name set to 'Millard Fillmore', hours to 19, hourly rate to $23.50.

code_references.snippet:
INITIALIZATION.
           MOVE "Millard"           TO EMP-FNAME.
           MOVE "Fillmore"          TO EMP-LNAME.
           MOVE 19                  TO EMP-HOURS.
           MOVE 23.50               TO EMP-HOURLY-RATE.

processing_logic.statement: Step 3 – Weekly Pay Computation: The program evaluates EMP-HOURS against overtime thresholds to set EMP-OT-RATE, then computes EMP-PAY-WEEK using the formula (Hours × Rate) × (1 + OT-Rate). With 19 hours and rate $23.50, no overtime applies and weekly pay = $446.50.

code_references.snippet:
PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           IF  EMP-HOURS >= 40
               MOVE .25 TO  EMP-OT-RATE
           ELSE IF EMP-HOURS >= 50
               MOVE .50 TO EMP-OT-RATE
           ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-OT-RATE.
           COMPUTE EMP-PAY-WEEK =
                (EMP-HOURS * EMP-HOURLY-RATE) * (1 + EMP-OT-RATE).

processing_logic.statement: Step 4 – Monthly Pay Computation: The program evaluates EMP-HOURS against the 150-hour reward threshold to set EMP-REWARD, then computes EMP-PAY-MONTH as (Weekly Pay × 4) × (1 + Reward). With 19 hours no reward applies; monthly pay = $1,786.00.

code_references.snippet:
PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           IF  EMP-HOURS > 150
               MOVE .50 TO  EMP-REWARD
           ELSE
               MOVE ZERO TO EMP-REWARD.
           COMPUTE EMP-PAY-MONTH =
                (EMP-PAY-WEEK * 4) * (1 + EMP-REWARD).

processing_logic.statement: Step 5 – Output Display: All computed and initialized fields are displayed to SYSOUT in labeled format, followed by a hard-coded personal message.

code_references.snippet:
SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".

processing_logic.statement: Step 6 – Program Termination: STOP RUN is issued after SHOW-OUTPUT returns, cleanly terminating the program.

code_references.snippet: STOP RUN.

dependencies.statement: No external programs, copybooks, CICS transactions, DB2 tables, or vendor modules are referenced. The program is entirely self-contained with all data hard-coded in WORKING-STORAGE. The unused field REC-COUNTER (PIC 9(1)) suggests a possible future dependency on record counting or looping logic that was never implemented.

code_references.snippet: 77  REC-COUNTER              PIC 9(1).

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           PERFORM INITIALIZATION.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-WEEKLY.
           PERFORM PAYMENT-MONTHLY.
           PERFORM SHOW-OUTPUT.
           STOP RUN.

error_handling.statement: There is no error handling implemented in this program. No ON SIZE ERROR clauses are present on COMPUTE statements, no FILE STATUS checks exist, no condition-name error flags are defined, and no EVALUATE/WHEN OTHER defensive logic is coded. Arithmetic overflow in EMP-PAY-WEEK (PIC 9(7)V99) or EMP-PAY-MONTH (PIC 9(7)V99) would cause silent truncation or an abend depending on the runtime environment.

code_references.snippet:
COMPUTE EMP-PAY-WEEK =
                (EMP-HOURS * EMP-HOURLY-RATE) * (1 + EMP-OT-RATE).

COMPUTE EMP-PAY-MONTH =
                (EMP-PAY-WEEK * 4) * (1 + EMP-REWARD).

downstream_effects.statement: The sole downstream effect is the console/SYSOUT print produced by SHOW-OUTPUT. No files are written, no database rows are updated, no messages are enqueued, and no other programs are CALLed. Any downstream consumer of this data (e.g., a payroll report or payment system) must read from SYSOUT or the program must be modified to write to a file or database.

code_references.snippet:
SHOW-OUTPUT.
           DISPLAY "Name: " EMP-NAME.
           DISPLAY "Hours Worked Per Week: " EMP-HOURS.
           DISPLAY "Hourly Rate: " EMP-HOURLY-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Bonus-Rate: " EMP-OT-RATE.
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Week: " EMP-PAY-WEEK .
           DISPLAY "Gross Pay Per Month: " EMP-PAY-MONTH .
           DISPLAY "Hi Chris - how's Loretta today?".
